Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in saas & startups. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

Product analytics and event pipelines

The source of product events, activation milestones and cohorts. We agree an event taxonomy with account-level grouping so every workflow reads the same definitions.

  • PostHog
  • Mixpanel
  • Amplitude
  • Segment or RudderStack
  • Firebase Analytics

Billing, subscriptions and payouts

Trials, renewals, mandates, failed payments and marketplace payouts. Their webhooks trigger conversion, recovery and reporting workflows, and card data stays with the provider.

  • Stripe Billing
  • Razorpay Subscriptions
  • Chargebee
  • RevenueCat
  • Stripe Connect or Razorpay Route

CRM and sales scheduling

Owner assignment, deals, tasks and outcomes for product-qualified accounts and churn risk. We write context into the CRM rather than asking reps to open another tool.

  • HubSpot
  • Salesforce
  • Zoho CRM
  • Pipedrive
  • Calendly

Help desk and in-app messaging

Where conversations, tickets and grievances live. The assistant and the moderation queue read from and write back to it, so agents keep one history per customer.

  • Intercom
  • Zendesk
  • Freshdesk
  • Zoho Desk
  • Crisp

Engineering and release tooling

Issues, releases and CI pipelines. Bug reports, feedback links, release notes and AI evaluation gates connect here.

  • Jira
  • Linear
  • GitHub
  • GitLab
  • Sentry

Data warehouse and reporting

Joins usage, billing, CRM and accounting data under locked definitions for health scores, cost per task and investor reporting.

  • BigQuery
  • Snowflake
  • Postgres
  • dbt
  • Metabase
  • Power BI

App stores and marketplace operations

Store reviews, subscription notifications, push delivery and supplier verification. We use the official APIs and follow each platform's policies.

  • App Store Connect
  • Google Play Console
  • Firebase Cloud Messaging
  • OneSignal
  • KYC and GSTIN verification APIs

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Activation rate

Share of new accounts or workspaces that reach the agreed value milestone within the agreed window after signup.

Why it matters: Activation predicts conversion and retention better than signups do, and it shows onboarding work where to focus.

Product-qualified account to opportunity rate

Share of accounts routed as product-qualified that become sales opportunities within the agreed period.

Why it matters: Shows whether the scoring rules find accounts sales can actually help, and when thresholds need adjusting.

Speed to first meaningful response

Elapsed time from a demo request or product-qualified signal to the first relevant contact by the assigned owner.

Why it matters: Interest fades during a trial; slow follow-up wastes the signals the product has already produced.

Trial-to-paid conversion

Share of trial accounts in a start cohort that become paying accounts by an agreed deadline after the trial ends.

Why it matters: The core self-serve revenue measure. Read it alongside refunds and cancellations so notices stay honest.

Involuntary churn

Paying accounts lost in a period because a renewal payment failed and was not recovered, as a share of paying accounts at the start.

Why it matters: Separates customers who wanted to stay from those who chose to leave, and sizes the payment recovery opportunity.

Net revenue retention

Recurring revenue at period end from a fixed starting cohort, including expansion, contraction and churn, divided by that cohort's starting revenue.

Why it matters: Shows whether existing customers grow or shrink, which investors ask about first for B2B SaaS.

AI escalation rate

Share of AI-handled conversations or tasks that required a human takeover under the agreed escalation policy.

Why it matters: Too low can mean the assistant keeps cases it should hand over; too high means it is not yet useful.

Cost per validated AI task

Model, retrieval, infrastructure and review cost divided by the AI tasks that passed acceptance checks in the period.

Why it matters: Connects AI quality to margin and shows which features, customers or model routes need attention.

Fill rate within agreed time

Share of marketplace requests that receive an accepted match within the agreed time window.

Why it matters: Liquidity is the marketplace's core promise; unfilled demand drives buyers away and supply follows them.

Report-to-action time

Elapsed time from a user report or complaint to a recorded moderation decision.

Why it matters: Shows whether trust and safety keeps pace with reports and with the grievance timelines set by India's IT Rules.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
